title: Resumable pagination & ergonomic batching helpers for embeddings + rerank across SDKs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add first-class, resumable pagination and ergonomic batching helpers for embeddings and reranking endpoints in Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Deliver code examples demonstrating streaming-friendly iterators, precise retry semantics across page boundaries, and a small canonical sample app that shows partial resume after interruption.
background: Customers want consistent behavior when listing large corpora for embeddings and performing rerank workflows that page results. Current SDK helpers differ between languages and often drop context on transient failures (e.g., timeouts mid-stream) or offer awkward tradeoffs between latency and throughput. This work aims to unify ergonomics and provide safe primitives for incremental processing, checkpointing, and backpressure-aware batching.
goals: Provide a resumable pagination primitive (cursor-based) for embeddings and rerank APIs in Python/TS/Go
Expose a high-level BatchIterator that transparently batches variable-length requests and honors per-language async semantics
Define retry semantics that are consistent across SDKs: idempotency guarantees, safe resume on transient failures, and clear guidance for developers
Ship cross-language examples and a small sample app demonstrating interrupted-resume and streaming-to-file
non_goals: Design a new server-side pagination protocol (we will use existing cursor/offset semantics)
Completely rewrite SDK transport layers (we will build on existing HTTP/streaming stacks)
Provide guaranteed zero-duplication semantics for user-provided mutable payloads (out of scope)
technical_approach: Implement library-level cursor wrappers that persist minimal resume tokens (server cursors or embedding batch offsets) and a checkpoint API for applications. Build language idioms: Python AsyncIterator + sync generator helpers; TS AsyncIterable with for-await example and a Node stream adapter; Go Channel-based iterator + context cancellation patterns. The BatchIterator will accept a max_batch_tokens and max_items window and will apply adaptive chunking based on per-model token estimates. Retries will be implemented with per-request idempotency keys and a boundary-safe rewind: when a failure occurs mid-batch, we retry only the failed batch using deterministic ordering and optional dedupe keys provided by the consumer.
api_changes_examples: Python example: EmbeddingsResumableIterator(tokenizer, client.embeddings.list, checkpoint_path='state.json') -> yields vector batches; checkpoint() persists last_cursor
TypeScript example: for await (const batch of sdk.embeddings.resumablePagination({cursor, pageSize})) { await processBatch(batch) }
Go example: iter := NewResumableIterator(ctx, client, opts); for batch := range iter.Ch() { handle(batch); if err := iter.Error(); err != nil { break } }
migration_notes: Existing SDK users continue to work with current pagination helpers. New helpers are additive under names resumablePagination / ResumableIterator / BatchIterator. Recommend gradual adoption for long-running ingestion jobs and rerank pipelines where restart safety is important.
testing_plan: Unit tests for iterator state transitions, integration tests against a staging server that can inject transient failures and resume tokens, e2e sample app that simulates process kill and restarts, performance test to validate batching latency/throughput tradeoffs. Add language-specific fuzz tests around token estimation.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge SDK PRs behind feature flag; 2) Publish beta packages for Python/TS/Go; 3) Run internal smoke tests on large-corpus ingestion jobs; 4) Promote to stable in sdk-2026.03 with docs and examples. Monitor customer feedback and error rates for 2 weeks post-release.
docs_to_update: API reference for sdk.clients.embeddings and sdk.clients.rerank
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose resumablePagination (TS), ResumableIterator (Go), EmbeddingsResumableIterator (Python) with consistent parameter names
Examples for interrupted-resume exist for each language and pass e2e test that simulates kill/restart
BatchIterator adapts chunk sizes and stays within configured token limits in 95% of test runs
Retry semantics documented and implemented: transient-only, configurable backoff, and safe per-batch retry
tasks: Design: finalize API shapes and naming in DESIGN doc (linked below)
Examples: sample app for each language showing resume and streaming to disk
Docs: write SDK docs and quickstarts
Release: publish beta packages and run internal validation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Clients may misuse checkpoint files causing duplicate processing. Mitigation: provide clear docs, sample patterns and optional dedupe key helper.
Risk: Increased memory usage when buffering batches for token estimation. Mitigation: enforce max_buffer_bytes and stream-to-disk fallback for extreme cases.
Risk: Cross-language API divergence. Mitigation: maintain a single canonical spec and run parity tests on CI.
